name: Afro House
summary: Straight 4/4 kick under a web of interlocking hand-percussion parts that answer each other - shaker-driven grooves, clave/cowbell timelines and conga/tom call-and-response - split between a deeper, percussion-forward lane (Black Coffee, Da Capo) and a stripped melodic lane (Keinemusik) that trades drum count for pad and chord space.

sounds.kick: Clean, rounded, mono deep-house kick (not distorted or gated); a harder 909-style kick suits the Afro-Tech-adjacent grooves.
sounds.snare: Understated layered clap on 2 and 4 (perc slot) pulled well back in level; constant light rim ghosts as a backbeat decoration rather than a snare backbeat.
sounds.hats: Closed hats sit under the shaker rather than replacing it; sometimes resampled lo-fi for the deeper, dustier grooves.
sounds.percussion: The genre's centre of gravity: a full velocity-contoured 16th shaker as the primary driver, clave/cowbell timeline instruments holding longer cycles, and conga/tom call-and-response phrases that answer each other rather than looping statically.
sounds.cymbals: Almost absent - no crash in this kit's afro_house patterns; a soft ride wash appears only occasionally in breakdowns.

machines: LinnDrum / Oberheim DMX - clean deep-house kick base
Roland TR-909 - harder kick, closed/open hat, ride for Afro-Tech-leaning grooves
E-mu SP-1200 - lo-fi resampled hats for the deeper, dustier lane
Roland TR-727 - clave, cowbell, conga and shaker patches
Roland CR-78 - softer analogue conga/bongo tones
Korg KR-55 / KPR-77 - period-adjacent latin percussion for the timeline instruments
Novation Drumstation / Quasimidi 309 - period rave-clap character pulled back for the perc slot
Real congas, djembe and shakers - genuine live hand percussion this drum-only library approximates with synthesized machines
